description: In kith-chat/src/space.rs:1467, space invite codes are generated as 8 random alphanumeric characters using rand::rng().sample_iter(rand::distr::Alphanumeric).take(8). With 62 possible characters per position, this yields log2(62^8) ≈ 47.6 bits of entropy. This is borderline for an invite code that may be long-lived and guessable by an adversary with network access. The RNG itself (rand 0.9 via rand_chacha) is a CSPRNG — the concern is the output length, not the generator quality. Recommendation: increase to at least 16 characters (≈95 bits) or use 128 bits from the CSPRNG encoded as hex/base64. The code is currently used as the human-shareable invite code; if shortness is required for UX, pair it with rate limiting on the join endpoint.
title: Space invite code: 8-char alphanumeric is ~47.6 bits entropy
